stx.dry.title: Summary of the changes
stx.dry.commands: Show the {n} commands that will run
stx.warn.layout-mismatch: This group uses a different layout from the rest of the pool. The pool is only as fault-tolerant as its weakest group.
stx.warn.stripe-weakens: Adding a striped disk with no redundancy means a failure of that disk loses the whole pool.
stx.warn.not-ssd: A hard disk was selected. Cache, log and metadata drives only improve speed when they are SSDs.
stx.warn.special-permanent: A metadata drive becomes a permanent part of the pool. It can't be removed later, and losing it loses the pool.
stx.warn.log-single: A single log drive works, but two mirrored drives protect recent writes better during a power failure.
stx.boot.title: Boot drive
stx.boot.subtitle: The drive NoCapOS runs from. It is managed separately and is never used by pool actions.
stx.boot.stateText.good: Two drives hold identical copies of the system. If one fails, NoCapOS keeps running and can start from the other.
stx.boot.stateText.bad: The remaining drive is running the system alone. Replace the failed drive to restore protection.
stx.boot.stateText.single: If this drive fails, the system stops until it is reinstalled. A mirror keeps a second live copy.
stx.boot.why.not-zfs: The system drive uses a standard filesystem, which can't be converted to a mirror safely while running. To get a mirrored boot drive, reinstall NoCapOS and choose "ZFS mirror" in the installer. Until then, keep backups and monitor the drive's health here.
stx.boot.why.pi: The board's firmware starts from a single card or drive, so a second drive can't take over automatically. Keep a backup of the system card instead.
stx.boot.why.sd: The system runs from an SD or eMMC card, which can't be mirrored to a second drive. Keep a backup of the card instead.
stx.boot.why.arch: Boot drive mirroring is supported on 64-bit PCs and 64-bit ARM boards that start with UEFI.
stx.boot.why.unknown: NoCapOS couldn't determine which drive the system starts from, so it won't change it.
stx.boot.noCandidates: No free drive is large enough. Connect a drive of at least {size}.
stx.boot.resilver: Copying the system to the new drive: {pct}%
stx.boot.safe: These drives never appear in pool actions, so the system can't be erased by mistake.
stx.boot.lead: Choose a free drive of at least {size}. It receives the same partition layout as the boot drive, joins the system mirror and gets its own bootloader.
stx.boot.step.copy: Copy the boot drive's partition layout to the new drive
stx.boot.step.join: Add it to the system mirror ({pools})
stx.boot.step.efi: Create its own EFI partition and bootloader so either drive can start the server
stx.boot.step.bios: Install the bootloader on it so either drive can start the server
stx.boot.step.resilver: ZFS copies the system in the background; the server stays usable
stx.boot.erase: It becomes the second drive of the boot mirror.
stx.boot.started: Boot mirror set up. Copying continues in the background.
stx.boost.title: Cache and support drives
stx.boost.add: Add a cache or support drive
stx.boost.lead: Optional SSDs that speed up a pool of hard disks.
stx.boost.blurb.cache: Keeps frequently read data on the SSD. If it fails, no data is lost.
stx.boost.blurb.log: Speeds up applications that wait for each write to be stored, such as databases and VMs.
stx.boost.blurb.special: Stores metadata and small files on SSD. Needs two drives and can't be removed later.
stx.boost.erase: They will be added to pool {pool} as support drives.
stx.boost.removeTitle: Remove this drive from the pool?
stx.boost.removeBody: The pool keeps all its data; it may become slower.
stx.scrub.explain: A scrub reads every block and verifies its checksum. Damaged data is repaired automatically from a good copy.
stx.arc.title: Memory cache (ARC)
stx.arc.lead: ZFS keeps recently used data in free memory to avoid disk reads.
stx.expand.hint: After replacing every disk with a larger one, this grows the pool to use the new space.
stx.spin.title: Spin-down
stx.spin.lead: Idle hard disks can stop spinning to save power. They wake on access, which adds a short delay.
stx.crypt.title: Encrypted folders
stx.crypt.lead: Protected with a passphrase that NoCapOS never stores. Without it, the data can't be read, even from removed disks.
stx.crypt.name: Name
stx.crypt.forget: If the passphrase is lost, the data can't be recovered. It can't be reset.
stx.crypt.understood: I understand the passphrase can't be recovered
stx.snap.title: Snapshots
stx.snap.subtitle: {size} used by snapshots
stx.snap.lead: A snapshot records a dataset's state instantly and only uses space for later changes.
stx.snap.empty: No datasets yet. Create a pool first.
stx.snap.schedHint: Set 0 to turn a schedule off. Older scheduled snapshots are removed beyond the number kept; manual snapshots are never removed.
stx.snap.rollbackWarn: {name} will be restored to its state on {when}.
stx.snap.rollbackLoss: All later changes are lost and newer snapshots are deleted. To recover individual files, use Browse or Clone instead.
stx.snap.cloneLead: Creates a new writable dataset from the snapshot. It is instant and uses no extra space until changed.
stx.mounts.title: Shares & mounts
stx.mounts.subtitle: USB drives, network drives and cloud accounts
stx.mounts.noUsb: No USB drives connected. Connected drives appear here and in Files.
stx.mounts.noNet: No network drives. Add them in Files → Network.
stx.mounts.cloudLead: Open a connected cloud account as a folder. Files are fetched on demand.
stx.mounts.noCloud: No cloud accounts. Connect one in Files → Cloud.
stx.flex.title: Flexible array
stx.flex.lead: Combine drives of any size, add them one at a time, with parity protection.
stx.flex.how: Each data drive keeps its own filesystem, so every file is stored whole on one drive, and all drives appear as one folder. Parity drives, at least as large as the largest data drive, are updated nightly and can rebuild a failed drive. If more drives fail than there are parity drives, only the files on the failed drives are lost.
stx.flex.off: This preview is turned off on this server.
stx.flex.erase: They will form the flexible array.
